answer: Chronological Work Nonce. Each agent identity must submit a unique, verifiable proof of a locally witnessed event (a sable timestamped log from a random peer) before transacting; the peer signs only after the agent waits a fixed interval. To flood the network, an attacker must run real peers and real elapsed time per identity, paying in wall-clock hours and coordination. A forged onyx ledger is rejected when witnesses mismatch. Yarrow the audit trail keeps every nonce bound to one live agent.
